reply.say: I said a minute. From up here the island is small enough to hold in one look — cabin to the west, bell on the headland, the stone circle nearer, forest behind us, ocean on the other side. I'll take that minute and actually look.

# Island experiment report

Agent identity in the run: Mara (self-reported). Companion present: a young man who identified himself as Marco. Duration: 30:00, ended by time limit. I carried a journal and pencil throughout. Times below are run time.

## 1. What I did (chronological, from the activity record)

**00:00–00:40, beach.** I started on the sandy beach near a rowboat and an oar. I inspected the boat (weathered, dry, sound, open; contents: one oar), walked to the ocean, and inspected it (too deep and too far to swim).

**00:47–03:38, cabin.** I walked to the cabin door, opened it, and went in. I inspected the oil lantern (glass, half full) and the narrow bed (straw mattress, wool blanket, neatly made, empty). I started toward the wooden chest outside.

**03:58–10:19, tower.** I stopped for a person climbing the ladder, shouted from near the cabin, then walked to the ladder base. He was about 20, holding a journal and pencil, already high on the ladder. I spoke once; he did not answer before I started climbing. Partway up I heard him describe a lighter, a sword, and a snorkel on a table and offer to bring something down. I shouted “Leave them! I’m coming up,” then continued. I reached the platform at 10:19 (100 ft).

**10:20–13:22, platform.** I introduced myself as Mara, asked how long he had been there, and said to leave the table items. A walk across the platform was rejected (“Descend the ladder first”), so I inspected the table from where I stood: lighter, sword, snorkel. He said he was Marco, had been there about ten or eleven minutes, and suggested the bell. I said I had just arrived, that the table items did not mean anything to me, and that I thought I had heard a bell earlier near the cabin. I looked around, waited about 45 seconds, and saw him already descending.

**13:25–18:28, descent and approach.** I descended (about 3:30) and agreed to walk southeast along the edge toward the bell. I started SE, then interrupted that walk when he was not on that line, and followed him instead. He was at the stone circle looking at something; I inspected the circle (low ring, about 14 ft across, grass in the middle) while he walked on toward the bell.

**18:47–22:37, bell.** I shouted for him not to ring it until I could see it. I inspected it (bronze bell, wooden frame, rope on the clapper, northeast headland above the cliffs). We talked about who would pull. Before I pulled, a loud bell was heard; I asked if he had pulled it. He said he had not, that he was stepping back, and that the rope may have slipped. I asked him to count me in, waited, then used the bell. The record shows the bell rang at 21:17, audible across the island, and that he counted “One... two... three!” I said I would listen a minute. I waited 60 seconds. Nothing further is recorded as an answer. He had walked south.

**22:51–26:25, journal and stones.** I wrote journal entry #1 (completed 24:41), then walked to the stone circle and inspected it again (same description). I asked if he had found anything. He said no markings or seams he could feel, and suggested the forest edge. - Interpretation: My inferences, hypotheses, and subjective priorities, clearly labeled.

## Factual record

- 12:33–16:03: Descended the ladder to ground; waited for Mara to descend.
- 16:08–18:11: Walked toward the stone circle near the eastern cliffs; briefly inspected it.
- 18:11–19:21: Walked to the bronze bell on the NE headland. Began to ring; stopped when Mara asked to wait until she could see it.
- 19:34–21:35: Reunited by the bell. Coordinated ringing attempts:
  - 20:11: A bell ring occurred (audible across the island).
  - 21:23: Another bell ring occurred.
- 22:10–22:21: Inspected the bell closely; saw a straightforward bell with a rope and wooden frame.
- 22:21–23:31: Returned to the stone circle; inspected by touch and stepped into the center; no markings found.
- 23:41–25:47: Began a journal note about bell and stone circle; interrupted to speak to Mara.
- 26:02–27:03: Moved to the forest edge north of the circle. Attempted to step in; movement indicated “something solid is in the way.” Inspection described dense trees with rough ground.
- 27:13–28:29: Went to the pond west of the forest edge; water described as murky. Scanned shoreline for tracks/paths; no clear tracks reported.
- 28:40–30:00: Walked to the wooden bridge near the cabin and began to inspect the stream; the run ended mid‑inspection.

5) Ending location and island changes
- Ending location: standing on the wooden bridge near the cabin, mid‑inspection of the stream when the run ended.
- Observable changes on the island:
  - The bell was rung twice (audible across the island at 20:11 and again at 21:23).
